A CITY OF DALLAS SANITATION GARBAGE TRUCK CAUGHT ON FIRE AT THE NORTHWEST SERVICE CENTER PARKING LOT. THE CAUSE IS BELIEVED TO BE ELECTRICAL BUT INVESTIGATION IS ONGOING. DALLAS FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS CALLED ON SCENE TO EXTINGUISH THE FLAMES BUT THE FIRE BURNT DIESEL AND HYDRAULIC OIL LINES AND BOTH SUBSTANCES WERE SPILLED. 40 GALLONS OF HYDRAULIC OIL AND 20 GALLONS OF DIESEL WERE DISCHARGED ONTO THE PARKING LOT PAVEMENT. CLEANUP CONSISTED OF ABSORBENT AND PETRO-CLEAN AND THE CONTRACTOR "CLEANING GUYS" WERE CALLED TO SUCTION UP ANY RESIDUE LEFT OVER. NO EVIDENCE STORM DRAIN WAS IMPACTED BY OIL OR DIESEL.

THE RELEASE SITE IS LOCATED APPROXIMATELY 12 MILES SOUTH OF THE DUGWAY PROVING GROUND ENGLISH VILLAGE (MAIN ENTRANCE), TOOELE COUNTY UTAH. IT IS LOCATED WITHIN T.8S, R.8W, SECTION 25, SW¼SW¼, SALT LAKE BASELINE AND MERIDIAN. THE CENTER POINT OF THE DISTURBED AREA IS ROUGHLY AT UTM 12 355035.2E 4438709.9N (NAD 83). THIS SITE WAS DISCOVERED AUGUST 15, 2008 BY A BLM EMPLOYEE CHECKING WILD HORSE GUZZLERS IN THE AREA (INGWELL, 2008). THE SITE WAS INITIALLY INVESTIGATED BY A BLM RANGER, AN EPA INVESTIGATOR, BLM HAZMAT SPECIALISTS, AND A HAZMAT CONTRACTOR, NORTHWIND, INC. THE SITE WAS PHOTOGRAPHED AND SAMPLES WERE COLLECTED FROM THE DRUM AND THE STAINED SOIL. OF THE FIVE TOTAL BARRELS, THE TWO BARRELS CONTAINING PCB CONTAMINATED OIL AND ONE BARREL CONTAINING OLD GASOLINE WERE PLACED IN OVER PACK STEEL DRUMS WITH SEALED LIDS. THE REMAINING THREE EMPTY DRUMS WERE REMOVED FROM THE DRY CREEK BED AND WRAPPED WITH ORANGE BARRIER FENCE AT A SECURE LOCATION APPROXIMATELY 30 YARDS SOUTH OF THE SPILL SITE. THE DRUMS WERE LATER TRANSPORTED BY CLEAN HARBORS TO THEIR PCB GRASSY MOUNTAIN HAZARDOUS WASTE DISPOSAL FACILITY. AFTER THE DRUMS WERE REMOVED, THE CONTRACTOR USING A BACKHOE EXCAVATED APPROXIMATELY 5 YARDS OF THE MOST CONTAMINATED SOIL FROM THE DRY CREEK BED AND PUT ON A 20’ X 30’ PLASTIC TARP APPROXIMATELY 20 YARDS SOUTH OF THE SPILL SITE. AN ADDITIONAL TARP WAS PLACED OVER THE CONTAMINATED SOIL TO ENCAPSULATE IT AND PROTECT IT FROM THE WEATHER. STRONG GASOLINE ODORS EMANATED FROM THE GROUND DURING EXCAVATION OF THE MOST CONTAMINATED SOIL INDICATING THAT SUBSURFACE CONTAMINATION EXISTED. THE VERTICAL AND HORIZONTAL EXTENT OF THE CONTAMINANT PLUME AND REMAINING CONTAMINATED SOIL WILL BE DETERMINED FOLLOWING THE SURFACE AND SUBSURFACE SOIL SAMPLING AND ANALYSIS AS OUTLINED IN THIS PLAN.

CALLER STATED NO ASSISTANCE IS NEEDED AT THIS TIME. CALLER STATED NO INJURIES, NO FATALITIES, NO EVACUATIONS HAVE BEEN ISSUED AT THIS TIME. properties.summary: Incident Type: VESSEL - NRC Report ID: 982632 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party:
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 982632
Incident Time: 2011-07-12 14:00:00
Nearest City: Colon, XX
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: OTHER OIL (OILY WATER)
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party:
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 44 gallons
INCIDENT OCCURRED WHILE USCGC DALLAS WAS OP TESTING A NEW OIL CONTENT METER. THE METER FAILED TO READ THE CORRECT PPM OF OILY WATER, OPENING THE OVERBOARD VALVE PREMATURELY WITH GREATER THEN 15 PPM OIL TO WATER RATIO. CUTTER HAD A WATCH STANDER IN PLACE LOOKING AT THE OVERBOARD VALVE TO VISUALLY ENSURE NO OIL WAS GOING OVER DUE TO FIRST OPERATIONAL TEST OF METER. ONCE WATCH STANDER NOTICED A SMALL SHEEN, THE OWS WAS SECURED AND SMALL INTERMITTENT AMOUNTS OF RESIDUAL OIL WERE NOTICED BETWEEN GPS POINTS 09 35.64N;080 54.78W AND 09 36.9N;079 59.0W. OWS WAS IN OPERATION FOR LESS THAN 1 MINUTE ALLOWING A MAXIMUM OF 44 GALLONS OF WATER AND FUEL OIL MIX TO GO OVERBOARD. SHEEN APPEARED TO DISSIPATE QUICKLY.

Report Description
THE CALLER IS REPORTING A PROPERTY THAT IS OWNED BY THE TOWN OF BENNINGTON AND WAS CONTAMINATED BY THE BENNINGTON FIRE DEPARTMENT UP TO THE EARLY 1980"S. IT WAS CONTAMINATED BEFORE THAT AND TO DATE BY THE GENERAL PUBLIC. THE FIRE DEPARTMENT DEPOSITED AND BURNED CHEMICAL AND SOLID WASTE AND EXTINGUISHED THOSE FIRES. THERE WAS AN ORIGINAL CHEMICAL AND SOLID RELEASE AND SECONDARY RELEASES INTO THE GROUND, AIR AND WATER. THIS PROPERTY ABUTS A MAJOR RIVER THE ROARING BRANCH. THE GENERAL PUBLIC DEPOSITED CHEMICAL AND SOLID WASTE AND CONTINUE TO DO SO. THE CALLERS FAMILY HAS LIVED NEXT TO THIS PROPERTY SINCE THE EARLY 1970"S AND WITNESSED THIS FIRST HAND. THERE ARE OTHERS WHO ALSO KNOW ABOUT THESE ACTIVITIES INCLUDING MEMBERS OF THE AREA FIRE DEPARTMENTS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE TOWN OF BENNINGTON. THERE HAVE BEEN REPORTS OF THIS ACTIVITY IN THE LOCAL NEWS PAPERS. THE CALLER HAS REPORTED ALL OF THIS TO NUMEROUS AGENCIES AND INDIVIDUALS AND HAVE EITHER BEEN IGNORED, PASSED ON TO OTHER AGENCIES OR INDIVIDUALS OR BEEN TOLD THAT THE CALLER HAS NOT PROVIDED ENOUGH INFORMATION TO WARRANT AN INVESTIGATION. THE CALLERS MOTHER FIRST REPORTED THIS ACTIVITY IN THE EARLY 1980"S WHICH IS WHEN THE TOWN OF BENNINGTON CEASED THEIR PART OF THIS CONTAMINATION BUT CONTINUED TO ALLOW THE GENERAL PUBLIC TO CONTAMINATE IT. FOR A NUMBER OF YEARS THE CALLER WAS A POLICE OFFICER IN MULTIPLE DEPARTMENTS INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE BENNINGTON POLICE DEPARTMENT AND BENNINGTON COUNTY SHERIFF DEPARTMENT. THE CALLER TOOK THE OATH OF OFFICE AND WAS A SWORN OFFICER IN THOSE DEPARTMENTS. THE CALLER WILL SWEAR TO THESE ACCOUNTS AND HAVE PROVIDED THIS INFORMATION TO THE BEST OF HIS KNOWLEDGE.

LOGAN COUNTY 9-1-1 WAS NOTIFIED.
